sections.title: WORKOUT
lines: Training Through Menopause: What Does the Evidence Tell Us?

For years, women approaching menopause heard the same advice: walk, stretch, and pick up light weights. The research tells a different story. Declining estrogen accelerates the loss of muscle, strength, and bone while raising cardiovascular and metabolic risk, and the best response is not gentler training.

lines: How Women's Nutritional Needs Really Change With Age (Part 3 of 3)

Nutrition advice for women gets more complicated by the year, with a different set of rules for every phase of the menstrual cycle and a fresh wave of warnings once perimenopause hits. But female physiology isn't as fragile or as complicated as the internet would have you believe. Here's what actually changes with age, and how to eat and train to protect muscle, bone, and metabolic health at every stage.

sections.title: FIGHT GONE BAD
lines: How do you perform the “Fight Gone Bad” workout?

Perform 1 minute of work at each of the 5 stations. Move immediately to the next station after 1 minute. The clock does not reset or stop between exercises. One-minute break is allowed before repeating each round. One point is given for each rep, except on the rower where each calorie is one point.
How do you score the “Fight Gone Bad” workout?
*Score is the total cumulative number of repetitions completed of all movements in all 3 rounds.*
